provider_if_inherited: Productivity suite provider (SYS-01); accounting SaaS vendor (SYS-05)
implementation_statement: The owner is the only user of every system: one named account in SYS-01, SYS-05, and the Prime A portal, and one laptop sign-in. Gap: a local administrator account that the IT consultant created in 2025-05 was still enabled until 2026-08-05, and authorized users and devices are not written down.
evidence: SYS-01 user list; laptop account list (P07); P03 G-001

implementation_statement: Planned by 2026-09-30: a standard (non-administrator) account for daily CAD, email, and browsing; the administrator account is used only to install approved software and change settings. Today the owner works in the administrator account.
The laptop locks after 5 minutes idle with a blank screen and needs the password or fingerprint to unlock. The phone locks after 1 minute.

The only remote access is sign-in to SaaS services over TLS with MFA. No remote desktop or remote-support tool is installed on the laptop. Gap: sign-ins are not monitored and SYS-01 browser sessions stay signed in for 90 days.
evidence: SYS-01 sign-in settings; laptop remote settings

implementation_statement: The phone has a passcode, biometric unlock, and device encryption. Gap: CUI email attachments can be opened and cached on the phone. From 2026-11-30 the phone is used only for MFA and non-CUI email; SYS-10 will not be installed on it.

Approved external systems are the Prime A portal (SYS-06) and, after 2026-11-30, SYS-10. Gap: CUI was stored in SYS-01 and pasted into a commercial AI chatbot (SYS-09); there were no written rules for external systems before POL-01.

The owner completed Prime A's 30-minute supplier cybersecurity briefing in 2025, which did not cover CUI handling or insider threat. Planned by 2026-10-31: a CUI handling course, an insider threat awareness course, and an annual security awareness course, with certificates kept.

SYS-01 records sign-ins, file access, and sharing events (inherited; 180-day retention on this plan). The laptop keeps default operating system logs. Gap: the events to log are not defined, laptop logs roll over in a few weeks, and the router keeps no logs.
evidence: SYS-01 audit settings; laptop log settings

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: No log has ever been reviewed. Starting 2026-10, on the first working day of each month the owner reviews SYS-01 (then SYS-10) sign-in and download activity and the laptop security log against a one-page checklist and records the review.
The POA&M (P07 poam.csv) lists every SP 800-171 requirement not met, with milestones and dates. It is the plan of action that SP 800-171 3.12.2 requires and the source of the date-to-110 in SPRS.

The laptop host firewall, disk encryption, screen lock, and automatic updates are on. Gap: no documented baseline settings for the laptop, phone, router, or printer; the router still used its default administrator password until 2026-08-05 (P07).

Project files sync to SYS-01 with 30-day version history (inherited). The owner copies a full laptop backup to a USB drive each week. Gaps: the USB drive is not encrypted and sits in an unlocked drawer; restores have never been tested; CAD license files are not backed up.
evidence: SYS-01 version history; backup drive check (P07)

implementation_statement: MFA protects the SYS-01 administrator console (authenticator app). Gap: local administrator sign-in on the laptop uses a password only. SYS-10 will use a hardware security key for the owner's administrator role.
evidence: SYS-01 security settings; laptop sign-in test (P07)

implementation_statement: MFA is required for network access to SYS-01 and the Prime A portal. Gap: SYS-05 (FCI only) uses a password only; MFA is turned on by 2026-09-15.

The owner chooses passwords and the SYS-01 provider enforces length. Gaps: passwords for 14 accounts are kept in an unencrypted spreadsheet in SYS-01; the laptop password is 8 characters; the router used its default administrator password (P07). Planned by 2026-09-15: password manager, 14-character passphrases, spreadsheet deleted.

Planned by 2026-10-31: obtain a DoD-approved medium assurance certificate (252.204-7012(c)(3)), register for DIBNet, and keep the P08 report checklist with Prime A's contact for the incident report number (252.204-7012(m)(2)(ii)). Today the owner cannot submit a DoD report.

The P08 runbook for CUI exfiltration was adopted on 2026-08-31 with a contact list. Gaps: not yet walked through; image preservation for 90 days depends on the IT consultant and an on-call forensics firm not yet engaged.
Printed CUI is cut in a cross-cut shredder next to the printer. Gaps: the laptop replaced in 2025 is still in a closet and has not been sanitized; the printer's stored jobs have never been cleared.

The home office has a lockable door and the house has a monitored alarm. Gaps: the door is usually unlocked while household members are home, a spare key hangs in the kitchen, and printed drawings stay on the desk.

Planned by 2026-09-15: a paper visitor log for anyone other than the owner who enters the home office (including the cleaning service and the IT consultant), kept one year and reviewed monthly; visitors are escorted and CUI is locked away first.

This short-form SSP, adopted 2026-08-31, replaces the 2025 template. It describes the boundary, asset categories, and how each SP 800-171 requirement is met; the requirement-level statements are the current_state column of P03 gap-analysis.csv. It is updated before any boundary change (SYS-10 migration).
The first evidence-based risk assessment was completed on 2026-07-24 using SP 800-30 Rev. 1 (P01). It is repeated each July and before major changes.

No vulnerability scanning has been done. Planned by 2026-10-31: a monthly authenticated scan of the laptop with a commercial scanner the IT consultant sets up, plus a monthly check of CAD software, router, and printer firmware versions.

Prime A operates SYS-06. Gap: CUI is held in SYS-01, a commercial offering that is not FedRAMP Moderate authorized or equivalent, and CUI was pasted into SYS-09. SYS-10 (FedRAMP authorized at Moderate or higher) was ordered on 2026-08-31; the provider's customer responsibility matrix will be referenced in this plan.
evidence: SYS-01 service terms; SYS-10 order and FedRAMP Marketplace listing (P09 Part B)

implementation_statement: The router blocks unsolicited inbound traffic and the laptop host firewall is on. Gaps: the laptop and printer share one flat network with family devices, guests, and a smart TV; outbound traffic is not monitored. A separate business network is planned by 2026-10-31.

The portal and SYS-01 use TLS. Gap: Prime A engineers sometimes email CUI drawings, and email between providers uses opportunistic TLS only. After migration CUI moves only through the portal or SYS-10.

Encryption is used for the laptop disk, the phone, and SaaS connections. Gap: none of these is confirmed to use a FIPS-validated module in an approved mode; the USB backup drive is not encrypted. SYS-10's FedRAMP package states FIPS-validated encryption; the owner will turn on the laptop's FIPS mode and buy a FIPS-validated encrypted backup drive.
The laptop disk is encrypted and the provider encrypts SYS-01 data at rest. Gaps: the USB backup drive is not encrypted; the disk recovery key is stored in SYS-01 next to the data.
Operating system updates are automatic on the laptop and phone; SaaS vendors patch their services. Gaps: CAD software is two releases behind and router firmware has not been updated since 2024.
Built-in antivirus scans in real time, scans USB media when connected, and updates signatures automatically. The owner keeps it on and acts on alerts.
